claim: Agent performance depends on a legible repository, enforceable architecture, isolated workspaces, executable feedback, and versioned plans.
observed_pattern: Humans design the environment and feedback loops while agents execute and review work.
precondition: Repository state, tests, logs, metrics, and UI are accessible to the agent.
failure_mode: Underspecified environments, inaccessible knowledge, architectural drift, and human QA bottlenecks.
control: Repository maps, AGENTS.md routing, invariant checks, worktree-local runtime, plans, and observability.
metric: PR throughput, task duration, test coverage, architecture violations, human attention.

claim: Deliverables in an issue tracker can be the durable control plane for continuously running coding agents.
observed_pattern: Organize work around outcomes and issue state rather than interactive sessions or PR count.
precondition: Clear task states, isolated workspaces, agent tools, CI, and recoverable runs.
failure_mode: Human context switching, stalled sessions, forgotten work, and fragile last-mile integration.
control: Issue-backed objectives, one workspace per task, restart on stall, CI watching, and review packets.
metric: Landed outcomes, stalled or abandoned work, time in state, human interventions.
applicability: direct with GitHub substitution for Linear

claim: Long-horizon agents need controlled workspaces, explicit instructions, tools, and sandboxed execution.
observed_pattern: Keep the model-facing harness separate from the controlled execution environment.
precondition: A sandbox can restrict filesystem, network, process, and lifetime boundaries.
failure_mode: Tool use escapes intended scope or makes unsafe environmental changes.
control: Controlled sandbox and explicit workspace/tool boundaries.
metric: Task success, policy violations, recovery rate, execution cost.
applicability: direct principle; implementation optional in v0.1

claim: AI-native engineering moves agents from isolated code suggestions toward planning, implementation, testing, review, and deployment support while humans focus on intent and higher-order judgment.
evidence_status: official_guidance; examples and results are self_reported_claim
observed_pattern: Delegate well-specified execution; retain human direction for ambiguity, architecture, and durable tradeoffs.
precondition: Written goals, planning artifacts, AGENTS.md, tests, and review criteria exist.
failure_mode: Agents receive mechanical tasks without enough product or system context, or humans remain the inner-loop bottleneck.
control: Outcome clarity, planning, repository instructions, executable feedback, and risk-aware review.
metric: Accepted outcomes, first-pass quality, review effort, defect and rollback rate.

claim: Agents independently accomplish multi-step workflows through tools and should start with the simplest architecture that fits, with guardrails and bounded human intervention.
observed_pattern: Use one agent by default; add orchestration only when complexity requires it; escalate on high-risk actions or failure thresholds.
precondition: Tools and instructions are well defined and intervention boundaries are explicit.
failure_mode: Needless multi-agent complexity, unlimited retries, or sensitive actions without oversight.
control: Simple composable patterns, guardrails, retry limits, and exact high-risk gates.
metric: Task success, retry count, escalation precision, latency, cost.

claim: An agent evaluation result is inseparable from its harness, environment, budget, validity checks, and the claim it is intended to support.
observed_pattern: Record the tested system and resource budget; check reward hacking, contamination, broken tasks, refusals, and evaluation awareness.
precondition: Evaluation tasks, harness, tools, safeguards, retries, and scoring are disclosed.
failure_mode: Headline scores overstate or understate capability because the setup changed or the task is invalid.
control: Comparable harnesses, explicit claims, validity review, intermediate artifacts, and budget reporting.
metric: Success distribution, attempts, tokens, wall time, cost per successful outcome, validity exceptions.

claim: Successful agentic systems usually start with simple, composable patterns and add complexity only when it measurably helps.
evidence_status: engineering_evidence from customer and internal practice
observed_pattern: Match workflow or agent architecture to task uncertainty; do not begin with a framework-heavy swarm.
precondition: The task and feedback loop can be characterized.
failure_mode: Framework complexity obscures failure, raises latency and cost, and reduces debuggability.
control: Start simple, evaluate, and add routing, parallelization, or evaluator loops only for demonstrated need.
metric: Task success, latency, cost, error localization.

claim: Long-running work across context windows benefits from an initializer, incremental progress, and explicit artifacts for the next session.
observed_pattern: Persist goal, plan, progress, verification, and next action outside the session.
precondition: Work exceeds one context window and the repository can hold durable state.
failure_mode: Context loss, premature completion, duplicate work, and a broken environment inherited by the next session.
control: Initializer, incremental changes, progress file, clean state, and end-of-session handoff.
metric: Resume success, repeated work, incomplete tasks, verification continuity.

claim: Context is a finite resource; effective agents need the smallest high-signal context assembled and refreshed over the loop.
observed_pattern: Use progressive disclosure, just-in-time retrieval, compaction, and structured notes instead of a giant prompt.
precondition: Knowledge is discoverable and can be routed by task.
failure_mode: Context pollution, stale instructions, lost goals, or crucial facts omitted from attention.
control: Small stable entry point, routed references, structured memory, and context refresh.
metric: Context size, retrieval usefulness, repeated discovery, task success, cost.

claim: A lead-worker multi-agent system improves breadth-first research when tasks are independently searchable, but coordination, evaluation, and reliability become first-order problems.
observed_pattern: Parallelize independent branches and keep synthesis and citation responsibilities explicit.
precondition: The problem is decomposable and parallel search value exceeds coordination cost.
failure_mode: Runaway spawning, duplicate search, uneven effort, citation loss, and high token use.
control: Lead agent, bounded delegation, saved plan, independent trajectories, citation pass, and production observability.
metric: Coverage, citation accuracy, task success, token use, wall time.
applicability: direct for parallel research; not a universal topology

claim: Filesystem and network sandbox boundaries can reduce repeated permission prompts while increasing practical autonomy and safety.
observed_pattern: Move routine safety from per-command approval to enforceable environment boundaries.
precondition: Allowed files and network destinations can be defined before execution.
failure_mode: Approval fatigue, prompt injection, broad filesystem access, and uncontrolled egress.
control: OS sandbox, filesystem isolation, network isolation, and explicit boundary exceptions.
metric: Permission prompts, blocked violations, task completion, security incidents.

claim: Agent evaluation should combine outcome checks, transcript or trajectory checks, code-based graders, model graders, and calibrated human judgment.
evidence_status: engineering_evidence from internal and customer deployments
observed_pattern: Define task, trial, grader, transcript, outcome, harness, and suite separately; run repeated trials for nondeterministic work.
precondition: Representative tasks and observable end states exist.
failure_mode: Final text claims success when environment state is wrong, or one passing run hides variance.
control: Outcome-first graders, multiple assertions, repeated trials, trajectory review, production monitoring.
metric: Task success, tool accuracy, latency, tokens, cost, error rate, grader agreement.

claim: Session, harness, and sandbox can be independent interfaces so implementations change without losing durable work or coupling state to one machine.
observed_pattern: Preserve stable role and work interfaces while treating model, harness, and execution host as replaceable.
precondition: Session logs and artifacts are stored outside an ephemeral worker.
failure_mode: A failed or stuck container destroys work state; harness assumptions become obsolete as models improve.
control: Append-only session, replaceable harness, replaceable sandbox, stable APIs, and recovery from live state.
metric: Resume latency, lost work, harness change regression, worker failure recovery.

claim: Planner, generator, and evaluator separation can improve long-running builds, but every harness component is a potentially stale assumption that must earn its cost.
observed_pattern: Treat the plan as a hypothesis and remove or add harness components through controlled evaluation.
precondition: Evaluation criteria make quality gradable and the application can be exercised end to end.
failure_mode: Bulky, slow, expensive scaffolding; evaluator drift; components retained after models outgrow them.
control: Ablation, structured handoff artifacts, planner-generator-evaluator roles where measured.
metric: Outcome quality, evaluator agreement, latency, cost, component lift.
applicability: direct as a method, not doctrine

claim: Agent risk is driven by nondeterministic paths, untrusted data, and the sensitivity of available tools; autonomy level alone is not the risk score.
observed_pattern: Classify data flow and tool effects; apply stronger isolation, taint handling, and time-of-use approval when untrusted data can reach sensitive actions.
precondition: Tools, data sources, trust boundaries, and downstream effects are inventoried.
failure_mode: Indirect prompt injection steers a sensitive tool or delegated authority is broader than the task.
control: Least functionality, sanitization, isolation, taint tracing, and approval for hazardous effects.
metric: Sensitive actions, tainted paths, blocked calls, approval precision, incidents.

claim: Production agent evaluation should measure the full trajectory, tool usage, outcome, reasoning efficiency, and cost rather than model scores alone.
observed_pattern: Instrument agent runs end to end and align custom metrics with the actual workflow.
precondition: Plans, calls, observations, outcomes, and resource usage can be recorded safely.
failure_mode: A strong base model fails in integration, loops, uses the wrong tool, or completes at unacceptable cost.
control: Trajectory capture, task-success grading, tool-call checks, efficiency and domain metrics.
metric: Task success rate, tool call accuracy, steps, latency, tokens, cost.

claim: Prompt-based defenses and model judges are insufficient enforcement for agent access, command execution, egress, and secrets.
observed_pattern: Keep deterministic access controls outside the model and remove persistent secrets from the execution environment.
precondition: Infrastructure can enforce identity, sandbox, network, and secret boundaries.
failure_mode: Prompt injection yields arbitrary commands, data exfiltration, or credential reuse.
control: Access control, sandboxing, default-deny egress, short-lived secrets, and package validation.
metric: Policy violations, egress attempts, secret exposure, containment and recovery time.

claim: AI amplifies the strengths and weaknesses of the surrounding delivery system; tool adoption alone does not create high performance.
observed_pattern: Optimize the organizational system, feedback speed, platform quality, and user value alongside AI use.
precondition: Delivery performance and organizational capabilities are measured together.
failure_mode: More code or higher local productivity increases instability, rework, or downstream review load.
control: Small batches, strong feedback, quality internal platforms, user focus, and stable priorities.
metric: Throughput, change stability, lead time, recovery, rework, user value.

claim: Multi-agent systems improve parallelizable tasks but can degrade sequential work and amplify errors; topology should follow decomposability and tool density.
observed_pattern: Use a single agent for sequential high-dependency work and a centralized coordinator for truly parallel branches.
precondition: Task dependencies and tool count can be estimated before delegation.
failure_mode: Communication overhead fragments reasoning; independent agents amplify correlated errors.
control: Topology selection, bounded fan-out, centralized integration, and architecture evaluation.
metric: Task success, coordination messages, error amplification, tool density, cost.

claim: Creative program generation becomes reliable in scorable domains when automated evaluators select and evolve candidates.
observed_pattern: Open-ended generation can be paired with objective evaluators and an iterative search loop.
precondition: The outcome has a trustworthy, quantitative, repeatable score.
failure_mode: Plausible programs are accepted without proof, or a poor evaluator rewards the wrong behavior.
control: Automated evaluator, candidate history, repeated execution, and selection by measured outcome.
metric: Correctness, quality score, improvement over baseline, reproducibility.

claim: Agent evaluation should cover the overall interaction and be tailored to production goals rather than rely on one generic score.
observed_pattern: Build a representative scenario set and mix deterministic, rubric, safety, and operational checks.
precondition: Expected behaviors and critical scenarios can be stated.
failure_mode: A proof of concept passes demos but fails diverse real workflows.
control: Layered evaluators, representative datasets, release baselines, and continuous evaluation.
metric: Scenario pass rate, safety, groundedness, tool quality, production regressions.

claim: Passing tests can conceal chaotic or unsafe trajectories; process quality adds information beyond binary patch success.
observed_pattern: Keep outcome as the first gate, then inspect trajectory waste, regressions, missing verification, and ordering for diagnosis and trust.
precondition: Comparable trajectories and valid tests exist.
failure_mode: Lucky passes, blind retries, regression cycles, and missing verification are ranked as ideal work.
control: Process-level signals beside pass rate, multiple successful references, and regression analysis.
metric: Pass rate, lucky-pass rate, waste signals, rank change, verification coverage.
applicability: direct with caution against prescribing one path

claim: Prompts, instructions, and traces contain explicit and implicit behavioral rules that can be extracted, checked, and inverted into adversarial tests.
observed_pattern: Turn important agent instructions into regression and adversarial scenarios rather than trusting prose alone.
precondition: Instructions and traces are available in a reviewable form.
failure_mode: Specification drift and manual review cannot cover thousands of traces.
control: Rule extraction, trace evaluation, model comparison, and generated negative tests.
metric: Rule violations, trace coverage, adversarial test yield, model comparison.

claim: Coding agents produce better pull requests when issues are well scoped and repositories expose build, test, validation, and local instructions.
observed_pattern: Use Issues for clear outcomes and AGENTS.md or repository instructions for durable local context.
precondition: The agent can build, test, search, and validate in its environment.
failure_mode: Ambiguous issues, missing dependencies, and hidden conventions produce low-quality PRs.
control: Meaningful issue scope, repository instructions, preinstalled dependencies, iterative PR feedback.
metric: PR acceptance, build and test success, review iterations, time to merge.

claim: Rulesets can require pull requests, status checks, code scanning, and other conditions before a protected ref changes.
observed_pattern: Encode repository invariants in the control plane rather than depend on an agent or reviewer remembering them.
precondition: Required checks are trustworthy, scoped, and cannot be casually bypassed.
failure_mode: An agent edits workflow policy or bypasses a human convention and merges unsafe state.
control: Branch rulesets, required checks, restricted bypass, and protected refs.
metric: Check status, bypass events, failed merges, policy changes.

claim: Artifact attestations bind a release artifact to repository, workflow, commit, environment, and event, but provenance is not a security verdict by itself.
observed_pattern: Record and verify how releasable artifacts were produced; apply an explicit acceptance policy.
precondition: Builds run through a trusted workflow and consumers verify attestations.
failure_mode: A release cannot be traced to exact inputs, or provenance is mistaken for proof that content is safe.
control: Signed attestations, immutable transparency where available, and verification policy.
metric: Attestation coverage, verification failures, untraceable artifacts.
applicability: direct for future releases; not required for docs-only v0.1

claim: Long-running cloud agents shift developers toward problem definition, tool and environment design, and review of logs, video, and previews.
observed_pattern: Reviewable evidence packets reduce the need to reconstruct an agent session.
precondition: Agents run in isolated environments and can return runnable artifacts.
failure_mode: Synchronous handholding, local resource contention, flaky environments, and review overload.
control: Cloud workspaces, parallel runs, logs, recordings, live previews, and explicit review criteria.
metric: Agent-created PR share, review time, environment failure, accepted outcomes.
applicability: useful pattern; metrics not independent evidence

claim: Agent-native development asks the agent to run the inner loop from context and plan through implementation, validation, and a reviewable change.
observed_pattern: Specify demonstrable success and design the environment for automatic objective verification.
precondition: Tasks have observable acceptance criteria and a bounded environment.
failure_mode: Code generation moves the bottleneck to review and validation; wrong assumptions compound.
control: Clear outcome, plan, validation procedures, and trace of decisions.
metric: Validation pass rate, review effort, rework, time to accepted change.
applicability: direct method; task-size advice requires OpenBoa adaptation

claim: Machine-driven delivery needs programmatic deterministic deployment surfaces, isolated execution, durable workflows, previews, observability, and rollback.
observed_pattern: Extend the agent loop beyond code to a runnable environment and production feedback.
precondition: Deployments are immutable, previewable, observable, and reversible.
failure_mode: Manual console steps break autonomy; untrusted code escapes; model or provider failures stall work.
control: Preview per change, API and CLI surfaces, sandbox, pause-resume-retry, monitoring, rollback.
metric: Deployment success, preview verification, rollback time, cost, provider errors.
applicability: direct principle; Vercel-specific implementation is replaceable

claim: Green CI is not proof of production safety when change volume rises; safe autonomy needs standardized environments, staged rollout, automatic stop, and rollback.
observed_pattern: Pair pre-merge checks with canaries and operational guardrails that react to real behavior.
precondition: Production metrics and rollback paths are machine-readable and tested.
failure_mode: A change passes tests but causes load, retry, cache, or scale failures in production.
control: Incremental deployment, automatic canary halt, rollback, rehearsed failure recovery, and observation.
metric: Canary health, rollback rate and time, incidents, production regressions.

claim: As agent autonomy grows, verification must reach the actual user-visible environment; syntax and unit tests alone can miss convincing but nonfunctional interfaces.
evidence_status: engineering_evidence; self_reported runtime and cost claims
observed_pattern: Give an evaluator access to browser state, logs, database reads, and persistent test context.
precondition: The built application can run in an isolated browser environment.
failure_mode: Potemkin interfaces, compounding shortcuts, context pollution, slow or expensive computer use.
control: Layered checks, code-based browser automation, testing subagent, persistent REPL, logs and read-only state.
metric: User-flow success, defect catch rate, verification cost, autonomous runtime.
applicability: direct for UI canaries; metrics not independent evidence

claim: A coordinator can decompose independent work across isolated agent VMs, inspect trajectories, cap compute, stop straying workers, and integrate results.
observed_pattern: Delegation needs narrow scopes, isolated environments, verification, monitoring, and a single integration point.
precondition: Subtasks are independent enough to run in parallel.
failure_mode: Context accumulation, conflicting edits, runaway compute, and unverified subagent reports.
control: Coordinator, separate VM and test runner, trajectory visibility, compute monitoring, termination, and compiled evidence.
metric: Subtask success, conflicts, compute use, stopped runs, integration defects.
applicability: direct pattern; no evidence that it beats single-agent for all tasks

claim: Agents can be represented as visible first-class workspace users assigned to issues, teams, projects, and comments.
observed_pattern: Give agent work a durable identity, current assignment, and visible progress rather than treating it as an invisible chat session.
precondition: Work is represented in an issue tracker with agent attribution.
failure_mode: Humans cannot tell which agent is doing what or reconstruct responsibility across sessions.
control: Agent profile, issue assignment, comments, status, and lifecycle-specific integrations.
metric: Active assignments, time in state, handoff delay, abandoned work.
applicability: direct conceptual support for collaborator role; not legal personhood

claim: Humans and agents need the same dependable cross-repository, historical, and architectural context to work safely on large systems.
observed_pattern: Treat context infrastructure as shared working infrastructure, not a prompt attachment.
precondition: Authoritative code and history are indexed with access controls.
failure_mode: Shallow context causes misleading plans and unsafe cross-repository changes.
control: Shared code intelligence, versioned API, historical search, usage tracking, and permission-aware retrieval.
metric: Retrieval usefulness, wrong-context failures, cross-repo task success, tool cost.

claim: AI risk management is continuous across design, development, deployment, use, and evaluation and should align controls with organizational goals and risk tolerance.
observed_pattern: Govern, map, measure, and manage as a lifecycle rather than add a one-time approval checklist.
precondition: Objectives, affected systems, risk tolerance, roles, and evidence can be described.
failure_mode: Controls are detached from purpose, risks emerge after deployment, or responsibilities are unclear.
control: Continuous risk review, impact mapping, measurement, management, and explicit accountability.
metric: Risk events, control effectiveness, residual risk, review cadence, recovery.

claim: Excessive functionality, permissions, or autonomy lets ambiguous or manipulated model output produce damaging external effects.
observed_pattern: Minimize tool functionality and permissions, constrain autonomy by effect, and require authorization where necessary.
precondition: Tools and permissions can be scoped to the task and effect.
failure_mode: Direct or indirect prompt injection, hallucination, or a compromised peer drives an unnecessary sensitive action.
control: Least privilege, least functionality, input and output validation, authorization, and rate or cost limits.
metric: Denied calls, excess permission findings, unauthorized effects, resource consumption.

claim: Shared semantic attributes make agent, conversation, workflow, tool, usage, and evaluation telemetry correlatable across libraries and platforms.
evidence_status: standard; GenAI attributes partly development status
observed_pattern: Use common trace vocabulary when runtime instrumentation is added, while protecting message content.
precondition: A runtime emits traces and sensitive fields can be filtered or truncated.
failure_mode: Vendor-specific logs cannot be compared, or raw prompts leak private data.
control: Semantic conventions, stable identifiers, opt-in content capture, redaction, and versioned telemetry.
metric: Task and workflow traces, tool calls, token use, evaluation scores, privacy violations.
applicability: future runtime guidance; v0.1 remains skills-only

claim: Build provenance should state how an artifact was produced, with higher assurance when a hosted and hardened control plane generates signed evidence.
observed_pattern: Separate trusted control-plane evidence from tenant-controlled build steps and verify provenance against policy.
precondition: A releasable artifact is produced by a defined build platform.
failure_mode: Outputs are built from an unintended source or process, or the worker forges provenance.
control: Provenance, signed hosted builds, hardened isolation, and verification against expected source and workflow.
metric: Provenance coverage, verification failure, unexpected source or workflow, unsigned releases.
applicability: direct for packaged releases; adapted conceptually to PR evidence
